The core challenge in tactical response modeling is aligning multi-agent state transitions across different roles (attacker vs defender). Graph Episode Alignment formalizes this as a spatio-temporal point process where each episode starts from an on-ball anchor event. The alignment ensures that the same players maintain consistent identities throughout the sequence, enabling direct comparison of how defensive formations adapt to specific attacking actions. This construction naturally supports downstream tasks like classification and retrieval by providing a fixed-size input structure that captures the interaction dynamics.
